messages:
support-oncall: FYI escalating. Customer acme-media sees p99 generation ~10s and intermittent OOMs after a big batch embed run this morning. They pasted a stack with repeated \"alloc failed, falling back to slow path\" and a bunch of kernel retries. They say it started after a campaign of long-context requests (~8k tokens).
sam (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you drop their request IDs and a small repro? do we have node IDs where OOMs happened? any recent deploys? :eyes:
support-oncall: Request IDs: rq_9a3f,rq_9a40,rq_9a4b. Nodes: gpu-prod-31, gpu-prod-47. No infra deploys around the window per deploy-bot. Customer provided this quick repro curl that reliably triggers the higher p99 for them:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"\nA long context...\", "max_tokens":8192, "batch_size":16, "stream":false}'
```
They say reducing max_tokens to 2048 drops p99 back to normal.
alex (eng-sre): Looks like classic GPU memory pressure + fragmentation. On these nodes, slab allocator reports high external fragmentation and KV table growth. Can you grab the allocator counters: `slab_free_pct`, `slab_compact_threshold`, `kv_live_entries` and `kv_evictions` from /metrics on gpu-prod-31/47? Also `nvidia-smi` snapshot + dmesg for OOMs.
maria (eng-runtime): I pulled metrics for gpu-prod-31 from the window: slab_free_pct=9%, slab_compact_threshold=0.72, kv_live_entries=1.2M, kv_evictions=0. Looks like KV never evicted which explains growth. Batch_size 16 + long contexts -> lots of KV allocations per request, plus small allocation churn causing fragmentation.
sam (eng-runtime): Interesting — the allocator's compacter currently runs when slab_free_pct < 5% which is too late. Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) set runtime flag `slab_compact_threshold=0.8` (more aggressive compaction) 2) enable `kv_eviction_policy=LRU` for tenant acme-media 3) throttle large batches via rate-limit/profile to batch_size=4 for tenant for 6 hours.
support-oncall: Customer is open to temporary throttling; they need low latency for some requests but can delay bulk embedding jobs. I'll ask if they want a dedicated pool.
alex (eng-sre): Long-term: we should tune allocator fast-path to prefer in-place compaction for small live-frag segments and expose a background compaction window to avoid synchronized compaction during requests. Also consider a soft cap `kv_max_entries_per_tenant` to prevent unbounded growth. For immediate relief I'd also recommend rolling restart of gpu-prod-31/47 during maintenance window to force defrag of device memory (thermal/driver free).
maria (eng-runtime): I built a small reproducible test to surface the issue locally: run the attached script (pseudo):
```
# generates many long-context requests to fill KV
for i in 1..200:
  python loadgen.py --model rw-large --tokens 8000 --batch 12
```
It matches customer behavior and raises kv_live_entries and fragmentation.
dev-bot: deploy:control-plane v2.18.3 rolled at 2026-03-12T04:12:30Z (no changes to allocator).
sam (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) support-oncall to ask customer to pause bulk embed for 4h and accept temporary batch limit=4 + switch to quantized variant `rw-large-q4` for lower memory footprint. 2) eng-runtime to flip `slab_compact_threshold` to 0.8 on a canary node and monitor p95/p99. 3) eng-sre to schedule rolling restart of affected hosts in next maintenance window and collect `dmesg`/nvidia-smi snapshots. 4) infra product to consider `kv_max_entries_per_tenant` product knob.
support-oncall: I'll send the mitigation plan to the customer now and ask for permission to throttle.
alex (eng-sre): One-off trick if customer refuses restart: temporarily set `allocator.force_compact=true` on the node (causes short pause but frees fragments). Use only as last resort.
sam (eng-runtime): I'll open a canary patch PR that exposes `slab_compact_threshold` as a runtime knob and add more verbose fragmentation metrics. Will post PR link here when ready.
support-oncall: Customer approved throttling + quantized variant, asked if we can guarantee 95th latency under 1s — we told them we'll monitor and report.
maria (eng-runtime): Quick numbers from the canary flip on gpu-prod-31 (history): after lowering batch_size and enabling q4 variant p95 dropped from 1.8s->0.9s and p99 from 9.8s->1.6s within 30m. KV entries stabilized and kv_evictions started at low rate.
sam (eng-runtime): Great. Next: track this with a short postmortem and prioritize allocator compaction improvements for the next sprint.
support-oncall: closing loop with customer now. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
